definition: Generating all acoustic frames in parallel with explicit duration prediction (FastSpeech lineage) instead of frame-by-frame autoregression.
details: Generating all acoustic frames in parallel with explicit duration prediction (FastSpeech lineage) instead of frame-by-frame autoregression. Fast and robust against the skipping and repetition failure modes of AR decoders; the contrasting design pole to codec-LM TTS.

explainer.lead: Non-autoregressive TTS generates all acoustic frames in parallel with explicit duration prediction, rather than frame by frame. It is the contrasting design pole to codec-LM TTS, trading some naturalness for speed and robustness.

tiers.eli5: Instead of writing a speech one note at a time, the model decides up front how long each sound lasts and then paints all the sounds at once.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers use the FastSpeech-style pipeline: a duration predictor sets per-phone lengths, and a parallel decoder produces all frames, which makes inference fast and avoids skipping and repetition. Pitfall: duration prediction errors show up as rushed or stretched words, since there is no autoregressive loop to correct them.
tiers.paperLevel: Given a text sequence, a duration model assigns a frame count to each unit and the decoder emits all frames in one pass from the expanded sequence. Known limits: it can sound flatter than autoregressive models, and accuracy hinges on the duration predictor.

explainer.example: A voice assistant renders a sentence in one parallel pass after the duration predictor assigns each phoneme roughly its expected number of frames.
